When the equation __H2 + __Cl2 -> __HCl is balanced using the smallest whole-number coefficients, what coefficient goes in front of HCl?
explanation: Balancing H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl gives 2 H atoms and 2 Cl atoms on each side. A coefficient of 1 in front of HCl would leave only 1 H and 1 Cl on the product side, not matching the 2 and 2 on the reactant side. Coefficients of 3 or 4 overcorrect and no longer balance the equation with H2 and Cl2 each at a coefficient of 1.
hints: Count the H and Cl atoms on the reactant side first — there are 2 of each.
Whatever coefficient you place on HCl must supply that same number of H atoms and Cl atoms on the product side.

stem: The reaction 2Na(s) + Cl2(g) -> 2NaCl(s) is best classified as a:
explanation: Two simpler substances, sodium metal and chlorine gas, combine to form a single compound, sodium chloride — the defining pattern of a synthesis (combination) reaction. It is not decomposition, since that would require one compound breaking apart. It is not single- or double-displacement, since those require one compound reacting with an element or another compound to swap partners, which isn't happening here.
hints: Look at whether the reactants are combining into one product or a compound is breaking apart.
Two elements forming one compound is the hallmark of a synthesis reaction.

stem: When the equation __C2H6 + __O2 -> __CO2 + __H2O is balanced using the smallest whole-number coefficients (with C2H6 = 2), what is the coefficient of H2O, and what type of reaction is this?
explanation: Balancing gives 2C2H6 + 7O2 -> 4CO2 + 6H2O. Checking: 4 C = 4 C; 12 H = 12 H; 14 O on the left (7 x 2) equals 8 + 6 = 14 O on the right. So the coefficient of H2O is 6. This is a combustion reaction because a hydrocarbon (C2H6) reacts with O2 to produce CO2 and H2O. Choosing 4 confuses the CO2 coefficient with the H2O coefficient. "Synthesis" is incorrect because two separate products (CO2 and H2O) form, not a single compound. Choosing 3 doesn't actually balance the hydrogen atoms.
hints: Balance carbon and hydrogen first using the given coefficient of 2 for C2H6, then balance oxygen last since it appears in two different products.
A hydrocarbon reacting with O2 to form CO2 and H2O is always a specific, well-known reaction category.

stem: Aluminum metal is added to a solution of copper(II) sulfate, CuSO4(aq). Based on the charges of Al^3+ and SO4^2-, what are the predicted products of this single-displacement reaction?
explanation: Aluminum displaces copper from the sulfate compound, so the products are an aluminum sulfate salt and copper metal. Combining Al^3+ with SO4^2- requires charge-balancing: the least common multiple of 3 and 2 is 6, so 2 Al^3+ ions (total +6) pair with 3 SO4^2- ions (total -6), giving Al2(SO4)3. AlSO4 ignores charge balancing entirely and assumes a 1:1 ratio. Al3(SO4)2 has the subscripts reversed. AlCu and SO4 incorrectly assumes the two metals combine directly with each other.
hints: Aluminum takes the place of copper in the compound, so the new ionic compound is formed from Al^3+ and SO4^2-.
Balance the charges of Al^3+ and SO4^2- the same way you would for any new ionic compound, using their least common multiple.

stem: Aqueous sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) is mixed with aqueous calcium chloride (CaCl2). Based on common solubility guidelines, what is predicted to happen?
choices: No precipitate forms, since both possible products are soluble
CaCO3 precipitates, because carbonates of most metal ions (other than Group 1 and ammonium) are generally insoluble
NaCl precipitates, because sodium salts are generally insoluble
Both possible products precipitate together as a single solid
explanation: The possible double-displacement products are CaCO3 and NaCl. Carbonate compounds are generally insoluble except with Group 1 metal ions (like Na+) and the ammonium ion, so CaCO3 (calcium, a Group 2 metal) is expected to precipitate. NaCl, on the other hand, is a soluble sodium salt and remains dissolved. The first choice wrongly assumes carbonates follow the same broad solubility as nitrates or Group 1 salts. The third choice reverses which product is actually insoluble. The fourth choice misunderstands that only one of the two possible products is insoluble here.
hints: Identify the two possible new combinations of ions first: calcium with carbonate, and sodium with chloride.
Carbonate is one of the polyatomic ions with an important solubility exception — it is NOT generally soluble the way nitrates and Group 1 salts are.

stem: Solid ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3, decomposes upon strong heating to produce two gaseous products, N2O and H2O. Which set of coefficients correctly balances __NH4NO3 -> __N2O + __H2O, in the order (NH4NO3, N2O, H2O)?
explanation: NH4NO3 contains 2 N atoms (one in the ammonium part, one in the nitrate part), 4 H atoms, and 3 O atoms. With coefficients 1, 1, 2: N atoms = 2 on the left, and 2 (from N2O) on the right; H atoms = 4 on the left, and 2 x 2 = 4 (from 2 H2O) on the right; O atoms = 3 on the left, and 1 (from N2O) + 2 (from 2 H2O) = 3 on the right. Every element balances. The other coefficient sets fail to balance either the hydrogen or the oxygen atoms once checked carefully.
hints: Remember that NH4NO3 has two separate nitrogen atoms in its formula — one from the ammonium part, one from the nitrate part — so both must be tracked.
Balance nitrogen and hydrogen first, then check that oxygen also comes out equal on both sides.
